newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African mines to shrug off gold price drop.
newsitem.headline: S.African mines to shrug off gold price drop.

text.p: South Africa's gold mining sector has seen its shares slip on recent worries over the fall in the bullion price, but analysts said on Tuesday the industry would shrug off the fall.
The bullion price has dipped recently and earlier London gold fixed at $382.45, its lowest level since July 9, 1996, as a sell-off in New York on Monday rippled through Asia and into Europe.
But analysts said the dip would create only short-term negative sentiment in South Africa's gold mining industry.
"It is not a major change. We have expected gold to trade within this range," said one analyst who declined to be named.
At noon, the gold share index ditched 49.9 points, or 2.82 percent, to 1,718.3 points. Gold index futures were also down at 1,188/95 from 1,213.

Analysts said the drop in the bullion price would add to recent worries over labour relations, violence at the mines and haggling on wage negotiations. The firming of the rand would also hit the recently strong rand bullion price, they added.
Shares in several gold shares were down on Tuesday. By lunch Kloof Gold Mining Co. Ltd was down 170 cents to 40.60 rand, Vaal Reefs Exploration and Mining Co. Ltd was down 12.50 rand to 376.00 rand.
Western Areas Gold Mining Co Ltd fell 150 cents to 62.00 rand and Western Deep Levels Ltd was off 325 cents to 159.50 rand.

Mining houses also dipped slightly, though the Johannesburg Stock Exchange as a whole was down. Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd was off 400 cents to 276.00 rand and JCI Ltd was off just five cents to 43.00 rand.
Analysts said the longer term outlook for the industry was positive and would easily shrug off ups and downs in the bullion price. "It is just a cyclical blip," said one.
